transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-02-26 15:00 PST | Duration: 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Jon Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (Cobalt Eng Manager), Mike Dawson (Cobalt ML Eng), Ravi Menon (Cobalt Infra), Leah Kim (Cobalt Product)

Summary: quick recap at top - we went through the benchmark sheet Alex shared, looked at latency (p50/p95/p99) and throughput numbers and compared to Cobalt's baseline provider (CloudX). Some transcriptions are fuzzy.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): okay hi everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick run through the benchmark sheet, call out the wins, the gaps and next steps. Samira will walk the perf runs.
[00:16] Priya (Cobalt): thanks Alex, we'll also flag questions at the end, we're mostly interested in p95 and p99 for our user flows.
[00:24] Samira (Redwood SE): all right so slide one -- or rather sheet tab one, shows the baseline from CloudX and our POC numbers on the dedicated pool. Important to note we ran the same model family, 8k context, and two sequence lengths: 128 and 512 tokens.
[00:40] Mike (Cobalt): can you remind us of the instance types? I thought you said these were Ampere A100 equiv?
[00:47] Samira: yes so for the dedicated runs we used G5-like GPUs (NVIDIA A10-style), the baseline from CloudX was the customer's provided numbers on their 4xA100 cluster, so CPU and infra differences exist. some of the naming in the sheet is approximate.
[01:05] Priya: yeah the baseline was from our staging cluster, not prod, but it's the numbers we have.
[01:12] Samira: cool; looking at the 128 token flow, p50 is comparable: CloudX 42ms, Redwood POC 39ms. p95 we see CloudX 120ms vs Redwood 95ms, p99 CloudX 280ms vs Redwood 230ms. throughput wise, tokens/s at steady state CloudX ~1.1k, Redwood ~1.3k.
[01:38] Leah (Product): that's promising, what's causing the long tail p99 still?
[01:44] Samira: a couple causes, we seen a couple of kv cache misses and a small proportion of requests hit a cold path where the KV prefetch didn't trigger; also there are scheduling spikes when concurrent streams overrun GPU batching windows.
[01:58] Ravi (Infra): when you say KV cache does prefetch, is that in our sidecar or inside the infer runtime?
[02:05] Samira: it's in the runtime, but requires the request prefix to be consistent, in a couple samples your traces had slight tokenization differences which led to lower cache hit rates, so that amplified tail latency.
[02:20] Mike: oh interesting, so we might need canonicalization at client side to maximize cache hits.
[02:25] Samira: exactly.
[02:28] [02:30] Alex: just to call out the benchmark methodology - we tried to mirror request arrival process, but we did synthetic concurrency ramps rather than replaying your full production traces (we asked for them but haven't received the 24h sample yet).
[02:43] Priya: we'll send that by early next week.
[02:47] Samira: thanks. moving on to the 512 token tests: CloudX p50 110ms, Redwood p50 98ms; p95 CloudX 410ms vs Redwood 350ms; p99 CloudX 760ms vs Redwood 680ms. throughput difference shrinks due to longer generation costs but we still see ~15% better tokens/sec on Redwood for this workload.
[03:12] Mike: those are fairly consistent. Did you try quantized runs?
[03:16] Samira: yes, we did int8 runs. With int8 the p50 improves by 10-15% but we saw occasional decoding artifacts on a subset of prompts, likely due to quantization noise; we flagged those in the quality tab. There is also an int4 experiment we haven't fully stabilized.
[03:34] Priya: quality tradeoff is big for us, can we get a AB style eval on the customer prompt set?
[03:40] Alex: yes we'll run an AB eval across a representative prompt list; Samira will lead the quality runs, we'll attach diff examples in the sheet.
[03:48] Samira: note though, the quantized runs were on the dedicated pool; if you go to hosted shared infra the behavior can vary based on kernel selection.
[03:57] [04:00] Leah: what about batching? any specific recommendations?
[04:04] Samira: we found batch sizes 2-4 are the sweet spot for low latency SLOs given your p95 targets. Batch>8 starts to increase p95 too much for your interactive flows. We can also do dynamic batching with user-priority routing to protect the low-latency lanes.
[04:20] Priya: ok that seems reasonable.
[04:23] Alex: want to highlight the baseline mismatch risk again: CloudX numbers in sheet were collected on a different day with slightly different concurrency and different warmup. so absolute differences matter but trends are what we care about.
[04:37] Mike: under- stood. any notes on network/Egress?
[04:41] Samira: we measured network tail and it added ~8-12ms on CloudX tests (public egress), on Redwood Dedicated it's within your VPC so less noisy, but will depend on your peering. Ravi you'll need to confirm the VPC peering window.
[04:57] Ravi: noted. I'll check peering times.
[05:01] [05:10] Alex: okay let's flip to the error rate and CPU/GPU utilization charts — Samira?
[05:14] Samira: error rates were low across runs, but we saw a few OOM errors when batch spikes hit non-quantized runs on the baseline. Redwood's runtime uses memory-friendly kernels and continuous KV cache which reduced OOMs. GPU util for Redwood was 78% average vs CloudX 85% but with less variance (spikes). Lower variance helps tail.
[05:40] Priya: can you share the raw profs? the timeline view?
[05:43] Alex: yes those are in the perf_logs folder and we'll attach - link in the sheet.
[05:48] [06:00] Mike: curious about cost delta — tokens/s improvements are good but if Redwood is using more expensive instances does it still win on unit cost?
[06:09] Samira: good question. we ran a normalized unit-cost calc in the economics tab. For your workload with caching and batching, unit cost/token on Redwood POC was ~12% lower than baseline due to higher token throughput and cache hit savings; that assumes reserved pricing on the dedicated pool. If you run hosted on on-demand it's closer parity.
[06:33] Leah: what about quantization impact on cost?
[06:36] Samira: quantization reduces GPU memory and increases throughput so unit cost can drop another 10-20% but again quality checks matter.
[06:44] [07:00] Priya: any visible regressions in output quality for our top 20 prompts?
[07:04] Samira: we did a spot check, there were a handful of prompts where token selection shifted; we captured examples — see quality_tab row 3-8. We'll run a full AB across your provided prompt set once you share it.
[07:16] Mike: also want to understand tail mitigation - can Redwood fall back to a smaller model fast if large model latency spikes?
[07:24] Alex: yes we have automated fallback policies — model variants can be configured as a route-level policy. For critical low-latency endpoints you can route to menor phant smaller model as a graceful degradation.
[07:36] [07:40] Priya: are there compliance notes? our security team will want SOC 2 and audit log samples.
[07:45] Jon (CSM): we have SOC 2 docs and audit log exports; Alex will share the security pack link and a short README.
[07:52] Priya: great.
[07:55] [08:10] Ravi: for the on-prem test we mentioned previously, is there a package or an appliance?
[08:14] Samira: we have a private deployment bundle and a VPC install guide; for air-gapped there's an on-prem tarball and HSM integration notes, we can share the doc link. small differences in kernel builds might change perf by a few percent.
[08:30] Leah: can we get a run on sqs-like steady low traffic? our product flow has 60% interactive and 40% batch.
[08:38] Samira: yes we can run a mixed workload trace once you share the sample trace.
[08:42] [09:00] Alex: quick pause — any blockers on our side?
[09:04] Priya: just getting the production traces, and security sign-off timeline. otherwise good.
[09:10] [09:30] Samira: OK moving to a few outlier cases: there was one prompt pattern that caused a tokenization mismatch and blow up in token count, that inflated p99. we flagged those IDs in the sheet.
[09:47] Mike: interesting, can we deterministic tokenization on our clients?
[09:50] Samira: yes, we'll provide a recommended tokenization shim.
[09:55] [10:30] Alex: next steps recap in chat: we'll run AB quality evals, Samira will run the int8 stabilized run and share logs, Alex will send benchmark CSV, Cobalt will share prod traces and define SLOs.
[10:48] Priya: timeline ok, we'll aim to share traces by Monday.
[10:52] [11:10] Leah: do you folks support request-level priority? we want internal tooling to mark some requests high priority.
[11:15] Samira: yes request-level QoS is supported; we can annotate requests with priority and protect low-latency lanes.
[11:22] [12:00] Ravi: small note on monitoring: can we get token-level cost breakdown in the console?
[12:05] Jon: yes console will have per-route token cost and latency breakdowns; we can enable an extended retention pack if needed.
[12:14] [12:40] Mike: anything else on benchmarks?
[12:43] Samira: one more: we noticed your baseline had intermittent GC pauses on the staging side which increased tail -- we captured the trace and marked the times in sheet.
[12:53] Priya: ok we'll check.
[12:56] [13:30] Alex: okay let's confirm owners: Alex sends sheet + security pack; Samira sends perf logs and runs int8 and int4 experiments; Cobalt shares traces and decides on AB prompt set.
[13:52] Priya: noted.
[13:58] [14:30] Leah: can we set up the deep-dive with Ravi and your infra lead next week?
[14:34] Alex: yes we'll propose times in calendar, tentatively Wed 10am PT.
[14:41] [15:00] Mike: thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[15:03] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links. bye.

End: quick recap and links: benchmark sheet (link: https://redwood.ai/prod/benchmarks/COBALT-POC-2025-02-26), perf logs (attached), security pack (link), next call tentatively 2025-03-05.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-attribution (Unidentified Speaker), some product names transcribed inconsistently (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes as "Redwood Dedicate" or "deds"), and acronyms may be spaced (S A M L).
